name: Easton Glacier

waypoints.name: Park Butte / Schreiber's Meadow
waypoints.directions: Drive to the end of Forest Road 13 (Sulfur Creek Road), which ends at the Park Butte / Schreiber's Meadow trailhead at about 3,360 feet. From the parking area, pick up Park Butte Trail 603 and cross Sulfur Creek on a footbridge or log crossing near the start — this can become a genuine ford during peak snowmelt.

waypoints.name: Sandy Camp / Railroad Grade Camp
waypoints.directions: Take Park Butte Trail 603 across Sulphur Creek (a footbridge or logs, a ford at peak melt) and up through the meadow and forest switchbacks to Morovitz Meadow, the last running water. At the signed junction there go right on Railroad Grade Trail 603.2, up stone steps onto the moraine crest, and follow it with the Easton Glacier dropping away on your right to Sandy Camp, where the crest runs out near 5,900 ft.

waypoints.name: Mount Baker Summit
waypoints.directions: Rope up at the glacier edge and climb roughly north toward Sherman Peak, keeping climber's right of the main crevasse bands. Near 9,400 to 9,700 ft at the rim of Sherman Crater, cross the rockfall-swept slope quickly and trend west across the saddle to the foot of the Roman Wall, climb its 35 to 45 degree snow staying right of the rocky rib, then cross the summit plateau to Grant Peak.

approach: From the Park Butte/Schriebers Meadow Trailhead (~3,360 ft, end of FR 13/Sulfur Creek Road), the route follows Park Butte Trail 603. Cross Sulfur Creek on a footbridge/log crossing near the start (can be a ford in high water), then climb through Schriebers Meadow and forest switchbacks to Morovitz Meadows (~2 miles in). For the Easton Glacier route, leave the Park Butte trail here and bear right onto Railroad Grade Trail 603.2, which climbs the crest of a lateral moraine (the 'railroad grade') with the Easton Glacier dropping away on the right. High camp options are at established sites around 5,600 ft (roughly 3.75 miles from the trailhead) or at Sandy Camp, a cluster of rock-walled tent pads at the moraine's end near 5,900-6,000 ft where the maintained trail effectively ends and glacier travel begins. From Sandy Camp, gain the toe of the Easton Glacier, rope up, and ascend the broad glacier, generally staying climbers' right (east) of the major crevasse bands, to the base of the Roman Wall. Hazards: exposed moraine crest can be loose/exposed in wind, Sulfur Creek crossing can be difficult during peak snowmelt, and there is no reliable water source above Morovitz Meadows other than melting snow.
